Review complete. I read the standing SUPERBOSS instructions, then reviewed the actual checked-out PR #610 diff (not just the self-report) including files truncated in the pasted diff.

**Verdict: reject** (tier2 — requires human sign-off regardless).

Key finding: the new migration `drizzle/0268_sales_pipeline_dashboard_targets.sql` creates the org-scoped table `compliance.crm_sales_targets` with **no Row-Level Security at all** — no `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, no tenant-isolation policy, no service-role bypass policy, no index. Every other org-scoped table in this repo's history (verified against `drizzle/0101`'s identical pattern) carries all three. Since the app connects via the `app_runtime` role, which by this codebase's own documentation has no RLS bypass and depends entirely on RLS policies for tenant isolation, this table currently has zero DB-level defense — it relies solely on application code never forgetting an `orgId` filter. That implicates AGENTS.md Rule 9's named "multi-tenant RLS context" guardrail.

The rest of the feature (aggregation logic, tests, API route, page) is solid — I double-checked the month-format handling between the targets table and the trend chart, which looked like a mismatch bug at first glance but is actually handled correctly. Also flagged as secondary: the worker's own PROGRESS.md discloses `bun run build` never completed in their sandbox, so the production build is unverified. No `.github/workflows/**` changes in this diff.

`review-verdict.json` has been written to the workspace root with the full verdict.
